introduction: Explore Storm Port’s docks, streets, guilds and hidden outskirts; prepare the citysmith’s shield materials and Tchan’s four proofs.
orientation: The coast and road connect to Storm Port through its outer routes. Successful physical arrival records discovery; a travel message or a moving boat alone does not.

Tchan’s native greeting uses hi or hello as alternate words for one conversation. He accepts four exact items together: prison shackles, a captain’s badge, a verbeeg tooth and a smooth stone. His empty acceptance reply still has a mantle reward.

Tchan is currently stocked in the separate Monestary of Tranquility. Finding him there and discovering Storm Port are separate; his native bundle remains a Storm Port request. The old local monastery description is not proof he is stocked there.
The citysmith accepts a slab of granite and leather straps together for a shield. This request and Tchan’s request are independent, with no required greeting or order between them.

The death knight carries granite, and hidden straps are inside the closed harbourmaster’s desk. Open the desk, search and then GET the straps. Current native flags do not lock it despite its drawer prose.

The minotaur in the prison carries shackles; the verbeeg below the food shop carries a hidden tooth; the cliff golem carries a hidden smooth stone. Revealing a passage or object, opening it, recovering materials and accepted turn-in are separate actions.

The captain’s badge is stocked on the bridge of the older ship interior. Its current access route needs builder review. The operating ferries use different interiors; supplied exact materials remain legal for Tchan’s bundle.

Carry every requested material loose. Held, worn or nested items do not prepare a bundle. The four mantle proofs have native NORENT flags, so keeping them through logout differs from keeping a recorded accepted receipt.

Current preparation changes as items are acquired or spent. Supplied exact items also fit. Possessing a mantle or shield does not reconstruct an accepted request or prove first acquisition from its native source.

The current Seaspray and Stromvok ferries use their own tickets and route identifiers. New ticket purchases are unavailable while accounting is active. An old local ticket or the ticket handler’s timed message does not prove boarding, paid passage or destination arrival.

Tchan’s task-clearing prayer is also unavailable while accounting is active. Meeting teachers, shopping, hiring crews, repairing ships and renting need their own admitted outcomes; they do not complete these two requests.

The slaves and prisoners, graveyard, religious places, guilds, families and town defenses suggest wider stories. Builders must define lasting rescue, investigation, learning and restoration outcomes before they can award completion.

stories.title: Bring Tchan the four Storm Port proofs
stories.summary: Carry the complete requested bundle loose and offer it for a mantle. This request can be accepted independently of the other Storm Port turn-in.

steps.hint: The minotaur in the prison carries these shackles. Recover the exact item into loose inventory; a personal kill is not required by the native turn-in.
The captain carries this badge on the older ship bridge. Its current access route needs builder review; the operating ferries do not enter that interior. A supplied exact badge also fits.

The giant verbeeg carries a hidden tooth in the basement below the food shop. Reveal and opening admission, actual recovery and custody are separate; the native turn-in does not require a remembered carve.
The rock golem carries a hidden smooth stone on the cliffs behind the secret rocks passage. Search and current recovery are separate; the native turn-in allows a supplied exact stone.
Offer the complete exact bundle loose in one admitted turn-in. Current materials prepare this request; the accepted receipt records its completion independently of the other request.
